name: Cash–Landrum incident
description: A 1980 close-encounter UFO case in southeast Texas in which Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum, and Vickie's seven-year-old grandson Colby reported a diamond-shaped craft emitting flame and heat, escorted by approximately 23 military helicopters. The witnesses subsequently reported severe injuries consistent, in their physicians' view, with radiation exposure.
full_description: The Cash–Landrum incident took place on the evening of December 29, 1980, on a rural two-lane road (FM 1485 / 2100) in dense woods near Dayton, Texas, in the Houston exurbs. Betty Cash (age 51), Vickie Landrum (57), and Landrum's seven-year-old grandson Colby reported that as they returned home from a restaurant they encountered a large, diamond-shaped craft with a flat top and bottom, hovering above the road and emitting a downward cone of flame so intense that it heated the metal of their car. The craft was, according to the witnesses, escorted by approximately 23 helicopters in tight formation, including identifiable Boeing CH-47 Chinooks. In the days that followed, all three witnesses reported nausea, vomiting, headaches, sunburn-like skin reactions, blistering, and hair loss; Cash, who had spent the longest time outside the car, was hospitalized in a critical condition. The case became one of the most-cited 'physical effects' UFO encounters of the 20th century and is unusual for the substantial primary documentation of the witnesses' medical condition. Cash and Landrum sued the U.S. government for $20 million; the case was dismissed in 1986 by U.S. District Court Judge Ross Sterling on the basis that the United States neither owned the object nor operated the helicopters described. The principal investigator was MUFON's John F. Schuessler, an aerospace engineer at NASA's Johnson Space Center; the U.S. Army's own investigation was conducted by Lt. Col. George Sarran. Skeptics including Philip J. Klass, Curt Collins, and Brian Dunning have argued that the medical evidence does not require a UFO explanation and have raised questions about the timeline and corroboration.
origin: Single-incident case located on FM 1485/2100 between New Caney and Huffman, in Liberty County, Texas, with the encounter terminating near Dayton.

etymology.origin: Named for the principal witnesses, Betty Cash and Vickie Landrum.

timeline.event: Cash, Landrum, and Colby Landrum encounter the diamond-shaped craft and helicopter escort near Dayton, Texas
John F. Schuessler (MUFON) begins formal investigation of the case
timeline.significance: Case enters the UFO research literature

timeline.event: U.S. Congressman Ron Paul forwards Cash and Landrum's complaint to federal agencies on their behalf
Lt. Col. George Sarran of the U.S. Army Inspector General's office investigates and reports that no Army aviation unit was operating in the area at the relevant time
U.S. District Court Judge Ross N. Sterling dismisses Cash and Landrum's $20 million lawsuit
timeline.significance: Federal court rules that no U.S. agency was shown to have owned the object or operated the helicopters
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas

timeline.event: John F. Schuessler publishes The Cash-Landrum UFO Incident
timeline.significance: Definitive book-length treatment of the case from the principal investigator

timeline.event: Betty Cash dies in Birmingham, Alabama on the eighteenth anniversary of the encounter
timeline.significance: Her family attributes ongoing illnesses to the encounter; cause-and-effect contested by skeptics

related.name: Rendlesham Forest incident
related.description: Same-period (December 1980) close-encounter case with multiple witnesses

related.name: Travis Walton incident
related.description: Earlier close-encounter case with claimed physical effects on a witness

cultural_notes: Among UFO communities the case is widely treated as one of the strongest physical-effects encounters; in skeptical communities it is treated as a cautionary example of how illness narratives can attach to a misidentified event.

sources.title: Cash v. United States (Civil Action No. H-81-3441)
